sense: the written words of a book or document

terms.gloss: the text, what is written; a writing
evidence: Auct. Her. 1.19: cum scrīptō ipsō (Lewis & Short)
Quint. 1.1.15: in quō librō scrīptum hoc invenītur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Anything written: a writing, a work (scrīpta, see literature), and in the rhetoricians the letter of a text as against its intent, scrīptum et sententia.
The words themselves, as against the sense: ad verbum, word for word (Cic. Fin. 1.4).

terms.gloss: the text (of a book or passage)
terms.comment: Classically the connection, the run of the words (see context); the text itself from Dante on.

terms.gloss: text (on a screen, in a document)
terms.comment: Classically texture, the weave of cloth; of style, the joining of words (Quint. 9.4.13), and late the course of a narrative (Amm.): Lewis & Short.

phrases.latin: ex scrīptō et sententiā contrōversia nāscitur cum vidētur scrīptōris voluntās cum scrīptō ipsō dissentīre
phrases.english: a dispute over letter and intent arises when the writer’s wish seems to disagree with the text itself

sources: Lewis & Short: scribo · Lewis & Short: verbum · Lewis & Short: contextus · Lewis & Short: textus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. text. John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 260, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
